competitions.result: Fourth round — lost 2–0 away to Manchester City in a replay, after a 0–0 draw at Anfield.
Quarter-final — lost 3–1 away to Tottenham Hotspur in a replay, after a 1–1 draw at Anfield.
Winners — beat Borussia Mönchengladbach 3–2 on aggregate, winning 3–0 at Anfield before losing 2–0 away.

in.note: Joined in July 1972 and made ten competitive appearances during the season.

overview: Liverpool won the First Division and the UEFA Cup, securing their first league title since 1966 and their first European trophy. A goalless draw with Leicester City at Anfield on 28 April clinched the championship; they finished with 60 points, three ahead of Arsenal.

Kevin Keegan was the leading scorer with 22 goals in all competitions. He and John Toshack each scored 13 in the league, while summer signing Peter Cormack contributed ten goals across the campaign after joining from Nottingham Forest.

Liverpool reached the UEFA Cup final by beating Tottenham Hotspur on away goals. Against Borussia Mönchengladbach, two goals from Keegan and one from Larry Lloyd gave them a 3–0 first-leg win at Anfield on 10 May. A 2–0 defeat in the return on 23 May left Liverpool 3–2 winners on aggregate and completed the league and European double.

events.title: The league title returns
events.detail: A 0–0 draw with Leicester City at Anfield secured the First Division championship.

events.title: A three-goal lead in the final
events.detail: Keegan scored twice and Lloyd once as Liverpool beat Borussia Mönchengladbach 3–0 in the completed first leg at Anfield.

events.title: Liverpool win the UEFA Cup
events.detail: Despite losing the return leg 2–0, Liverpool won the final 3–2 on aggregate to claim their first European trophy.

researchNotes: Keegan scored 22 in all competitions. His league tally was 13, shared with Toshack; those are distinct categories.

The final was won 3–2 on aggregate, not 5–0 as one Liverpool anniversary article states. UEFA, RSSSF and the two match records resolve the discrepancy. The original first leg on 9 May was abandoned; the completed match was on 10 May.
Jimmy Case’s May 1973 recruitment is recorded with the incoming 1973–74 campaign, not among this season’s first-team contributors.

Peter Spiring is not copied from the 1973–74 transfer ledger into that season: the date printed there is March 1973. He is omitted from these selected senior moves rather than given an incorrect arrival season.
